_comment: Batteries-included architecture-gate rules for a React (Vite/CRA/Next) + Supabase app: UI → data hooks → services → lib/integrations, with exactly one Supabase client and edge functions composing a shared layer. Adjust the globs to your repo's folder names, then run `node scripts/ci/arch-gate.mjs --baseline > arch-gate.waivers.json` to grandfather existing violations. Rule names are stable identifiers — a waiver's 'rule' field must match one exactly.
_builtins_note: emptyCatch/swallowReturn are OFF: TFN uses documented graceful-degradation catches (e.g. catch { /* storage disabled */ }) which a regex can't tell from a real hide — error-handling judgment belongs to the judge-arch review, not the mechanical gate.

rules.name: UI must not access the database directly
rules.message: Data access inside a component/page. Route it through the hook/service that OWNS this data, so there is one read path and schema/RLS changes touch one file, not dozens.

rules.name: Services must not import UI or touch web globals
rules.message: Service/domain code leaks a web/UI concern and can no longer be tested or reused without a browser. Keep React/DOM at the boundary; pass plain data into the service. (src/lib holds legitimate web adapters and is not policed by this rule.)

rules.name: Exactly one Supabase client in the frontend
rules.message: A second Supabase client. There must be exactly one configured client (auth/session/storage config lives with it). Import the canonical client; never construct another.

rules.name: Edge functions must not hand-roll auth or read service-role secrets in the handler
rules.message: Auth/admin logic hand-rolled per function drifts and can't be hardened in one place. Use the shared request-auth + admin-client helpers in supabase/functions/_shared.

rules.name: Edge functions must not hand-roll CORS or responses in the handler
rules.message: Inline CORS/response shaping duplicated per function drifts (missing preflight headers silently fail requests). Use the shared cors/json helpers in supabase/functions/_shared.

rules.name: Edge functions must not hand-roll HTML stripping/sanitization
rules.message: A hand-rolled tag-stripping regex (`<[^>]*>` / `<[^>]+>`). Single-pass strippers are bypassable by nested reconstruction and mis-handle entities (CodeQL js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization, js/bad-tag-filter, js/double-escaping). Use the shared owner supabase/functions/_shared/html-to-text.ts (htmlToPlainText / stripActiveContent) — fixpoint + tempered match + `&`-last decode.

rules.name: ops_events writes go through record_event, never a direct insert
rules.message: A direct insert into ops_events bypasses record_event (the single write path) and drifts from the table shape: ops_events has no `source` column, so a top-level `source` made PostgREST silently 400-drop every email-v2 telemetry row (PGRST204, ADR-0060). Emit via supabase.rpc('record_event', { p_sink: 'ops_events', p_kind, p_severity, p_payload }) — the path the record-auth-* functions use — with event metadata in p_payload. Reads (.select) are fine. NOTE: this rule INCLUDES _shared/** because the writer is a CONSUMER of the record_event owner — unlike the handler-only edge rules above, which exclude _shared.

rules.name: Displayed stats must be live-derived, never read a stored counter table
rules.message: A displayed stat is being wired to a stored/denormalized counter table (course_completion_stats / network_stats_snapshots / welcome_flow_stats). Those freeze when their refresh job stops and drift when they have two writers (ADR-0050: Platform Signups sat at 768 for months because its snapshot's cron wasn't running). Read the LIVE count via the owning RPC — get_network_stats / get_course_completion_counts / get_welcome_flow_completion_count (requirements §6.13) — which counts the source-of-truth rows (profiles / journey_progress / course_completions / profiles.welcome_flow_completed_at).

rules.name: projects reads use explicit columns, never select('*')
rules.message: A select('*') on public.projects from the authenticated client. projects is COLUMN-SCOPED for `authenticated` (ADR-0056): select('*') expands to the four operational columns this role cannot read and fails Postgres 42501 / HTTP 403 — which shipped as "Project not found" on the application-resume page (ADR-0065). List the explicit non-sensitive columns the surface renders; the four operational columns (discord_role_id, discord_role_name, notion_repository_url, client_intake_url) come only from the get_project_internal_links RPC or the service-role public-project-detail edge function.

rules.name: Welcome Flow builds on the design system only (no shadcn ui, no lucide-react)
rules.message: The mandatory Welcome Flow must build on the TechFleet Design System (`@/design-system`) only — not shadcn `@/components/ui`, not `lucide-react` icons (ADR 20261009-welcome-flow-gate / requirements §13). Mixing the legacy shadcn stack into a greenfield feature drags a second component system and a data-access-in-component anti-pattern into new code. Use DS components + the DS `SvgIcon` atom / brand SVG assets. (No existing files match this glob — the welcome dir is greenfield — so this rule is proven by the fixtures in arch-gate.smoke.test.ts, not by any current violation.)

rules.name: welcome_flow_completed_at has exactly one writer
rules.message: An object-literal write to welcome_flow_completed_at outside its single owner. This column is set ONCE, server-side, by the mark_welcome_flow_complete() SECURITY DEFINER RPC, reached only through ProfileService.markWelcomeFlowComplete (ADR 20261009-welcome-flow-data-model, requirements §6.5). A second writer breaks set-once and is the ADR-0050 two-writer class. Reads (profile.welcome_flow_completed_at) are fine; only a `welcome_flow_completed_at:` assignment is forbidden. The generic updateFields allow-list must never include it.

rules.name: Welcome Flow imports SVGs as URLs, never via SVGR
rules.message: An SVGR-style SVG-as-component import in the Welcome Flow. This repo has no SVGR (adding it is a build dependency); import the unDraw-style Figma SVGs as a URL and render via `` / the DS `SvgIcon` atom (requirements §13). Proven by a fixture in arch-gate.smoke.test.ts (greenfield dir).
